gen-fs-merriweather-sans-fs-karma: Cozy sums up Merriweather Sans, whose big counters let you see right into each curve. Karma, a text serif with weighty stems and terminals clear of the stem, adds a trustworthy, classic counterpoint.
gen-fs-merriweather-sans-roboto-slab: Big-hearted letters meet sturdy ones: Merriweather Sans opens its curves wide while Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, stays structured. Merriweather Sans really earns its keep when it's big and brief.
gen-fs-new-title-cabin: Tall, chain-tight, and bold. New Title leads, then Cabin, a warm sans with open terminals, makes extended reading go down smoothly, its bent-tube letterforms never tiring the eye over time.

gen-fs-oswald-gf-domine: Oswald's tightly knit rows give it a strong, confident look all its own. And Domine, a text serif with compact ascenders and a breathing space inside every curve, handles the reading with a modest dip in its thin strokes.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-epunda-slab: Oswald sets a confident, tightly knit display line over a moderate lowercase. And Epunda Slab, a serif, contrasts it with tall rounded forms and a visibly gaping c, which is the pair's most striking quality.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-kosugi-maru: Kosugi Maru glows like neon tubing, with stroke ends set far apart. Under Oswald's confident, tightly knit heading, this plain sans keeps its stroke widths put from stem to curve, so paragraphs would move along smoothly.

gen-fs-oswald-gf-port-lligat-slab: Port Lligat Slab reads literary, with wide round counters like portholes. Shrink Oswald down and its tight, confident rows lose their punch, while the slab's hugging letters would still hold up if enlarged.

gen-press-start-2p-gf-cossette-titre: Retro pixel blocks sit over snug, low-profile text, each letter nestled close to the next. Press Start 2P is at its best big and brief, and Cossette Titre follows.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-headland-one: Old arcade charm over a dignified serif. Headland One has gently varied strokes and well-spaced letters, and next to Press Start 2P it brings a traditional gravity that makes the fun feel deliberate.
gen-press-start-2p-rubik: Soft and playful, Press Start 2P gives a retro, pixel-spaced heading with light modulation. And Rubik answers with big lowercase and round, open letters, which makes the fun feel easy to read.
gen-press-start-2p-work-sans: Work Sans reads crisp and current, its curve tips holding well apart and its strokes never swelling at the joins. Press Start 2P brings the pixel-toy fun on top, and the sans-serif below keeps a longer page moving without friction.
gen-righteous-fs-familjen-grotesk: Lively is the mood here: Righteous fills its lines with bowls drawn like bent steel rod, one steady thickness throughout. Familjen Grotesk takes over below with tall lowercase and half-open bowls, so a longer passage feels light and easy to keep reading.
gen-righteous-fs-trench-slab: Righteous bends every letter like thin steel rod, round and bold.  Trench Slab, a serif with hardly any gap between x-height and caps, sits beneath it with a dignified, compact steadiness that lets the display lettering stay the loud one.
gen-righteous-gf-asimovian: Asimovian reads friendly and plain, every lowercase letter tall. Its strokes keep a single width, which gives Righteous, with bowls that fill the line, a quiet partner that never competes for attention.
gen-righteous-gf-savate: Righteous bends its letters like cable, with no swelling or thinning anywhere. Savate follows with sturdy hairlines, open curves and a round o nearly the size of a capital, adding a light modulation that makes the display lines feel even more deliberate.
gen-righteous-poppins: Punchy rounds, steel-rod lines. Righteous fills its bowls to the edge, while Poppins keeps a plain sans body with loose, rope-like curves and tall sturdy lowercase, so the heading gets the spotlight and the text stays easy to follow.
gen-roboto-slab-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro reads clean and unfussy, its curves ending well apart and its strokes like bent steel rod. Roboto Slab does the sturdy, structured heading work with tall lowercase, while the plain sans below simply carries the text forward.
gen-roboto-slab-fs-merriweather-sans: Roboto Slab gives headings a structured, sturdy look, its tall lowercase making words feel large and solid. And Merriweather Sans carries that height into the text, with an open-eyed e that keeps a long page comfortable to follow.
gen-roboto-slab-fs-ranade: Ranade reads relaxed and organic, its weight shifting only slightly and its stroke ends set well apart. Roboto Slab is best at sturdy, tall-lowercase headings, whereas the plain sans below does its best work in a spread-out, gently lighter line.
gen-rubik-fs-karma: Friendly is the first word for Rubik, with its big x-height and bowls that feel open and inviting. Karma follows as a classic serif with a calm modulation, so size it modestly and it stays trustworthy beside that heading.
gen-rye-fs-paquito: Authoritative and vintage, Rye stands tall with hairline-tipped stems that give its lowercase a dark, sparkling texture. And Paquito, a confident text serif, is approachable and made for a quick read.
gen-shadows-into-light-fs-hoover: Friendly and inviting, with letters crowded like chalk on a full slate. Shadows Into Light is best at casual charm, while Hoover, a robust text serif, is happiest in quick bursts.
gen-shadows-into-light-mulish: Crowded chalk-mark letters give Shadows Into Light a hand-scrawled, friendly feel. Mulish, a modern sans with unmodulated strokes, sits beside it easily, so the scrawl feels approachable rather than messy.
gen-shrikhand-fs-literata: Shrikhand brings a commanding, warm display voice with plenty of weight behind it. And Literata, a sophisticated text serif with subtly varied strokes, hushes it down to a bookish murmur.
gen-shrikhand-fs-rowan: Shrikhand has commanding, warm display letters with a low-contrast heft that grabs the eye before anything else. Rowan, a friendly literary serif, wouldn't carry pages of dense text.
gen-silkscreen-fs-ranade: Lo-fi retro letters with room to breathe all around each one. Silkscreen and Ranade both love wide spacing, and the sans-serif's organic, slightly rubbery stroke warms up the whole retro mood.
gen-silkscreen-gf-actor: Lo-fi spaghetti lines, with space you can almost feel around each letter, make Silkscreen the loud one here. Actor stays clean and modern, a quiet foil with barely curled s curves.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kiwi-maru: Space around every letter that you can almost feel defines Silkscreen, with lines like spaghetti laid out flat. Kiwi Maru, a traditional serif with generous letterspacing, gives the retro look an editorial anchor.
gen-silkscreen-gf-special-gothic: Lo-fi and retro, with room around every letter that you can nearly feel. Special Gothic does open, rounded sans-serif friendliness best, while Silkscreen brings the swagger of spaced-out spaghetti lines.
gen-space-grotesk-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sophisticated, with wide-mouthed curves. Space Grotesk, a geometric sans-serif cut from single-weight strokes like a flat stencil, makes that quiet stroke contrast feel much sharper.
gen-space-mono-fs-ranade: Typewriter-stiff stencil letters up top, then a loose, stretched-out line below. Ranade's gentle taper and tall lowercase soften what Space Mono draws as a rigid ribbon.
gen-space-mono-montserrat: Montserrat reads wide and gliding, with generous curves that slide past quickly. Space Mono is best at being blunt and mechanical, while Montserrat does its best work being smooth and welcoming in a plain sans way.
gen-special-elite-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro keeps its curves open and its lines crisp, like bent steel rod under a worn, smudged headline in Special Elite. Be Vietnam Pro is the steadier half, and that gap is the whole appeal.
gen-special-elite-fs-hoover: Hoover reads sturdy and refined, with short ascenders and a generous opening into the e under Special Elite's scuffed, oversized lowercase. Expect a comfortable, unhurried read.
gen-special-elite-fs-nunito: Special Elite brings a scuffed, typewritten look with a wide-mouthed a, while Nunito's big round bowls and open endings take over below. Pages of it should feel friendly and easy going.
gen-special-elite-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters tight, with big counters and curves that refuse to close, a warm plain sans under the headline. And Special Elite's distressed, tall-filling lowercase stands out best when it is sized well above it.
gen-special-elite-fs-trench-slab: Worn and typewritten, Special Elite fills the line with oversized lowercase, and Trench Slab sits under it, dignified and compact. One does rough character best; the other does refined structure.
gen-special-elite-montserrat: Distressed and a bit rebellious, Special Elite fills each line with its wide-mouthed a. Montserrat is the smooth foil, with its wire-like glide, where the headline is gritty and knocked about.
gen-special-elite-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads precise and structured, its middle zone dominating the line with open throats on a, c, e and s. Against Special Elite's distressed look, the structure becomes the pair's best quality.
gen-syne-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Syne's x-height climbs almost to cap height, giving headlines a bold, experimental stripe of constant ink. And Be Vietnam Pro follows with open curves and a high mean line that read cleanly.
gen-syne-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab stands tall in its lowercase, grounded and a touch refined. Syne is best at looking like one bent wire, all smooth curves and no pinching, while the body does its best with sturdy upright letters.
gen-syne-fs-erode: Smooth wire-like curves up top, editorial dignity below. Syne is best at bold, pressure-free lines with a constant stroke, while Erode is best at a gentle ebb and flow of weight across a tall middle band.
gen-syne-fs-hoover: Syne draws a smooth, pinch-free line with no swell where its curves turn corners. And Hoover, refined and robust, reads steadily over time, its generous e openings and compressed ascenders keeping lines tight and sturdy.
gen-syne-fs-paquito: Syne has the steadiness of a drawn string, experimental and commanding at once. And Paquito, confident and approachable, sits quietly beneath with almost no gap between its lowercase and caps, so the two settle together easily.
gen-syne-fs-quicksand: Experimental from the first letter, Syne draws smooth, pinch-free curves. Syne is best at commanding, tall-x-height display lines, while Quicksand is best at approachable text with bulb-like bowls and open stroke ends.
gen-syne-fs-ranade: Experimental Syne keeps the arches of its r, n and m closely matched to their stems. And Ranade, gently shifting in weight with widely spaced letters, looks best given a little extra size.
gen-syne-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified and refined, its lowercase standing nearly level with the capitals. And Syne is best at a bold, followable outline of constant width, while the body is best at quiet, steady text.
gen-syne-gf-graduate: Smooth as bent wire, Syne leads, then Graduate follows, bookish and dignified, with generous white between its letters. Syne is best at bold display punch; Graduate at quiet, steady text.
gen-titan-one-fs-asap: Titan One is bold and playful, built from tube-like, constant-weight strokes. Asap works nicely at a modest size under big headings, its open c arcs and near-capital body height staying easy to follow.
gen-titan-one-fs-public-sans: Titan One has tubelike, constant-weight lines with stems and arcs in lockstep, bold and playful. Public Sans then settles into a hefty, trustworthy lowercase, with broad counters that keep paragraphs feeling open and steady.
gen-titan-one-inter: Inter keeps its lines smooth and open, like a tube cut clean. Under Titan One's chunky, brush-ended curves, a longer read goes down easily, with big counters and tall lowercase doing the work.
gen-titan-one-montserrat: Titan One stamps out chunky letters with a towering midzone and curves that stop like lifted brush strokes. Montserrat follows in a sans that glides under the eye, so a longer read feels spacious and friendly.
gen-titan-one-rubik: Rubik reads soft and clear, its lowercase looking big beside the capitals and its round letters holding up small. Shrink Titan One's heading down, though, and its constant, heavy line width starts to clog.
gen-tourney-fs-alpino: Cozy and casual, Alpino sits low and tall-bodied, so its ascenders look short and its curve endings stay well apart. Tourney, meanwhile, earns its keep when big and brief, stretching bulky letters across wide tracking.
gen-tourney-fs-karma: Tourney cuts every stroke with a pen that never changes pressure or angle. That suits loud, wide display lines, while Karma's gentle swell in each bowl and unhurried terminals suit sustained reading.
gen-tourney-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One reads literary and authoritative, slowing the eye to a leisurely walk with curvy, unclamped letters. Tourney is the shouter here, best when its wide-tracked, single-width strokes go big, while BhuTuka rewards lingering.
gen-tourney-gf-cascadia-code: Tourney stretches bold, athletic letters wide, every stroke cut to one width, and it's at its best loud. Cascadia Code is the opposite: a wire-like monoline with generous gaps, made for steady reading.
gen-tourney-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Heavy, stretched headline energy, then a surprisingly light follow-up. Mochiy Pop One hangs its very large lowercase on a long line like clothespins, so a longer read moves along smoothly.
gen-tourney-gf-open-sans: Tourney glows like neon glass, bold and athletic. Open Sans gives it a smooth, contemporary body with bulky lowercase proportions, so give the heading plenty of space to stretch out.
gen-tourney-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, its curves turning corners without any pressure swell and its c and s held well apart. And if Tourney's heavy, wide-tracked heading gets made small, its bulky letters crowd quickly.
gen-tourney-space-grotesk: Tourney shouts in wide-tracked, bulky letters, every stroke cut to one width. Space Grotesk follows in geometric sans with a moderate lowercase and counters that breathe, so paragraphs move along without any shouting of their own.
gen-ultra-archivo: Archivo opens its curves outward with a commanding x-height, giving text an approachable, editorial footing under the heading. Ultra does the dignified vintage work, with its mellow modulation; Archivo does the plain talking.
gen-ultra-fs-bespoke-sans: Vintage weight meets crisp restraint here. Ultra's closed, tightly packed letters hold the top, and Bespoke Sans lets generous space open around its curves, so a long passage feels sharp and unhurried.
gen-ultra-fs-public-sans: Ultra looks dignified and a bit vintage, with stems that outweigh its hairlines and a mild taper at every bend. Public Sans, a plain sans with a hefty lowercase, keeps long reading easy.
gen-ultra-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk draws each glyph as a ribbon of constant width, with counters that breathe, set under Ultra's close-packed serif. Over a long passage, that plain sans stays quietly geometric.
gen-unbounded-fs-fira-sans: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide, with a c that opens broadly and friendly. Fira Sans, with a larger-than-usual x-height and no thick-thin contrast, carries a long passage cleanly.
gen-unbounded-fs-gambetta: Oversized lowercase bodies, spread wide, define Unbounded. It brings friendly, contemporary presence up top, while Gambetta, a text serif, adds a graceful, restrained shift between thick and thin for the reading below.
gen-unbounded-fs-hoover: Friendly and contemporary, Unbounded spreads out wide. Hoover, a refined serif with a generous entry into the e and compressed ascenders, makes a long passage feel robust and sturdy.
gen-unbounded-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase and clearly opening e making words easy to catch. Its plain sans solidity under Unbounded's broad, friendly display letters is the pair's best quality.
gen-unbounded-fs-ranade: Friendly is the first word for Unbounded, spreading its oversized letters wide, while Ranade sets widely spaced type with only slight, organic shifts in weight. The pair's strength is how gently the sans body relaxes under it.
gen-unbounded-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab reads dignified, with rounded tall letters and gaping c shapes. Unbounded sits above it as the friendly, wide-stretched display voice, and that bold swap in character is the pair's real hook.
gen-unbounded-source-serif-4: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide and friendly across the top. Source Serif 4 follows as a text serif with a slight tightening at curve tops, which would keep paragraphs moving smoothly and soberly.
gen-unbounded-switzer: Switzer reads like wire bent into letters, tall and approachable. Beneath Unbounded's broad, stretched-out display forms, a long passage would feel light and tidy, with c tips that never crowd each other.
gen-unifrakturmaguntia-fs-public-sans: Gothic and clustered, like a banner from another century. Public Sans takes over with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, so a longer passage feels sturdy, trustworthy and easy to move through.
gen-vast-shadow-bitter: Every stroke in Vast Shadow is cut to one width, with no thin hairlines anywhere. Bitter, a slab-serif with big lowercase eyes and see-through s shapes, grounds that vintage flash so the two sit comfortably on the page.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro reads clean, its strokes like bent steel rod and its curve endings keeping their distance. Vast Shadow, with its vintage, tall-ceilinged letters, probably wants the larger size while this sans-serif stays modest below.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-familjen-grotesk: Vintage showpiece meets lively workhorse. Vast Shadow's tubing-like strokes have no hairlines at all, while Familjen Grotesk adds tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, so the page feels playful yet orderly.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-karma: Karma keeps its terminals well clear of the stem and its thick-thin shifts quiet. Vast Shadow's curves never thin at the turns, so beside this classic serif the heading feels bolder and the text more settled.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Vast Shadow draws attention with its tall, vintage letters, each stroke cut to one width and spaced generously. Pilcrow Rounded does the quieter work, with big counters, warm curves and tight spacing that make text feel snug.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, forming a heavy-looking band of text with letters held open rather than curled shut. Vast Shadow's thin, tube-like strokes give it a vintage lift, so a larger heading size would let each one show.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-savate: Vintage and eye-catching, Vast Shadow cuts every stroke to one width. Savate, a sans with open jaws on its curves, gives those uniformly heavy round letters a gentler partner, its verticals and bowls differing only slightly.
gen-vast-shadow-mulish: Vast Shadow cuts every stroke to a single width and leaves generous space around each letter, a vintage, eye-catching look. Mulish then reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph, its open curves never snagging.
gen-vast-shadow-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads in a precise, structured way, its slab-serif middle zone dominating the line. And down the page, Vast Shadow's rope-like vintage strokes above make that steady texture feel all the more grounded.
gen-work-sans-fs-erode: Bent tubing meets editorial dignity, with Work Sans holding a single gauge through every curve. Work Sans is best at crisp open curves, but Erode is best at a gentle ebb and flow of weight.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-chillax: Fat round bowls attach to the stem by hairline joins in Yeseva One, vintage and bookish. Chillax draws a spaghetti-like line, smooth as pen-plotter ink and relaxed enough to keep reading.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-literata: Literata reads like a sophisticated serif, its thin lines sturdy and its thicker ones only slightly heavier, with wide-open curves. Under Yeseva One's snagging fat stems, that text flows gently.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy and hefty, Public Sans lays down a solid sans body with broad, open counters beneath Yeseva One's fat bowls. Swollen stems and needle-thin joins up top, sturdy low-contrast strokes below.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-roundo: Fat round bowls on hairline joins make Yeseva One the dramatic, vintage half of the pair. And Roundo, cut like a fixed-width router bit, does the quieter work of keeping small counters unclogged.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-synonym: Yeseva One gives each letter a heavy trunk and whisper-thin branches. Synonym, a sans-serif drawn with technical-pen steadiness, lays a constant-ink stripe beneath, its generous curve openings keeping that bookish drama in check.
gen-yeseva-one-sora: Sora moves with a blunt round-tip marker feel, its c and s staying widely parted at every turn. That blunt marker against Yeseva One's rope-thick stems is the real draw.
gen-young-serif-fs-bespoke-sans: Young Serif looks plain and friendly, refined without any fuss. Bespoke Sans leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, and that sharp, refined body is what makes the pairing work.
gen-young-serif-fs-roundo: Roundo reads neutral and geometric, every small counter left unclogged. Young Serif brings the refined, friendly serif shapes above, while Roundo's sans runs as a plain stripe of constant ink beneath.
gen-yuji-mai-fs-rowan: Tight-lipped and measured, Yuji Mai spaces each word out with openings so slight the letters feel nearly sealed. And Rowan opens every curve wide, literary and friendly, a face to sip rather than gulp.
gen-zen-dots-clash-grotesk: The body text reads clean and approachable, as if drawn with a fixed-width nib. Clash Grotesk carries the running text, while Zen Dots, with lots of room around each letter, owns the tech-flavored attention up top.
gen-zen-dots-fs-alpino: Zen Dots gives every letter lots of room, a tech-flavored but friendly display voice. But Alpino, cozy and casual, stands much taller in the lowercase, with curve endings kept well apart.
gen-zen-dots-fs-asap: Zen Dots is tech-flavored and friendly, with room around each letter. Asap, a sans-serif whose c forms read as open arcs and whose body height nearly matches the capitals, gives the heading a readable partner.
gen-zen-dots-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Lots of room surrounds every Zen Dots letter, whatever the weight. Be Vietnam Pro, strokes like bent steel rod and a high mean line, keeps pages of text moving smoothly, curve endings never touching.
gen-zen-dots-gf-faculty-glyphic: Faculty Glyphic is a modern, professional sans-serif with clear openings in its rounded letters. And Zen Dots supplies the display character, tech-flavored and friendly, with lots of room around each letter.
gen-zen-dots-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans is a modern, precise sans built from monoline strokes, curve endings kept well apart. Zen Dots above, tech-flavored and friendly, loosens things up with lots of room around each letter.
gen-zen-dots-sora: Zen Dots leaves lots of room around every letter, with openings that stay generous at every weight. Sora takes over with precise, geometric strokes like neon glass, no swell at the corners.
gen-zodiak-cabin: Zodiak's strokes swing hard from heavy to hairline. Cabin sits beneath it like bent tubing, a warm sans with open endings that carry you down a long page without any fuss.
gen-zodiak-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Sharp contrast, then a smooth glide. Zodiak is at its best when its thick-and-thin strokes look dignified, while Be Vietnam Pro does its best work holding a tall, tidy line of sans-serif text.
gen-zodiak-fs-bespoke-sans: Dramatic weight up top, crisp restraint below. Zodiak's stark thick-to-hairline strokes set against Bespoke Sans, with its sans-serif curves pulling away from the stem, make a pairing of sharp opposites.
gen-zodiak-fs-familjen-grotesk: Stately strokes meet a lively, open-sided body. The strongest thing here is the gap between Zodiak's pronounced thick-and-thin rhythm and Familjen Grotesk, whose tall lowercase stays quick and level.
gen-zodiak-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad, open counters that make it sturdy. And Zodiak handles the drama, throwing dignified swings of heavy and hairline where the sans-serif body just gets on with the text.
gen-zodiak-fs-quicksand: Heavy strokes and hairlines share every Zodiak letter, which gives it an authoritative air. And Quicksand, a plain sans with bulb-round bowls and uniform bars, makes that drama feel friendly instead of stern.
gen-zodiak-fs-ranade: Zodiak leads with dignified, high-contrast strokes that look carved and confident. Ranade follows as a plain sans with barely shifting weight and widely spaced letters, so the page moves from drama into a loose, organic line.
gen-zodiak-fs-synonym: Zodiak sets bold strokes against hairline partners in every letter, and it sounds authoritative doing it. Synonym stays level and dependable.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-giga: Dramatic serif, flat sans. Lexend Giga spaces its single-weight letters generously, so a long passage moves slowly and smoothly beneath Zodiak's heavy-and-hairline headings.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-tera: Zodiak looks heavy and thread-thin at once, and that gives it real authority up top. Lexend Tera spreads out below, reading like stepping stones.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-zetta: Heavy stems framed by hairline strokes give Zodiak its dignified, authoritative bite. And Lexend Zetta runs wide and tall-bodied in a sans-serif of constant width, so a long page moves along smoothly, unhurried and open.
gen-zodiak-gf-orbit: Sharp, weighty, razor-edged. Orbit sits beneath Zodiak as a sans-serif of uniform, rope-like strokes, letting the heading's thick-thin drama stand out while the text keeps each character floating apart.
gen-zodiak-inter: Inter reads smooth and tube-like, with big counters. Zodiak does bold stems and razor-thin horizontals best, while Inter's horizontals match its verticals, which keeps text steady and easy to follow.
gen-zodiak-mulish: Thick downstrokes sit beside hairline crossbars in Zodiak, a serif with real authority. Mulish follows in a plain sans with large, modern shapes and uniform strokes, so a long page feels friendly and unfussy.
gen-zodiak-sora: Sora is precise and geometric, with a constant stroke. Its plain sans lines have no pressure swell at the curves, which gives Zodiak's swelling, hairline-tapering stems a sharp, dignified foil.
gen-zodiak-work-sans: Work Sans is a plain sans with an unmodulated outline, a high mean line and c tips held well apart. A long page of it goes down quickly.
ibm-plex-serif-ibm-plex-sans: IBM Plex Serif has a literary, authoritative voice, with gentle weight shifts along each curve (fine for, say, a birthday invitation). IBM Plex Sans takes over as a technical, approachable sans-serif with a wide channel into every bowl.
jetbrains-mono-inter: Developer-minded and contemporary, JetBrains Mono sets fixed-width, loosely strung characters whose terminals stay open like scissor blades. Inter then carries the text as a smooth sans-serif, its big counters and tall lowercase making a long stretch glide by.
josefin-cabin: Precise and neutral, Josefin Sans keeps its lowercase well under the ascender tops, with strokes that look cut from wire (say, an empty state illustration). Cabin's bent-tubing warmth sits comfortably beneath it.
libre-baskerville-manrope: Wide, loose and dignified, with authority to spare. Libre Baskerville spaces its letters generously, and Manrope's bright curve openings and steady pen line give a sans-serif that stays approachable.
lora-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans talks softly, with open curves in every small letter. Lora stands above it as a serif heading with a brush-stroke feel and only slight pressure variation, which gives the soft sans below a more authoritative voice to answer.
merriweather-poppins: Sturdy serif meets crisp, modern sans. Merriweather brings mid-level stroke contrast and a dignified weight to the heading, while Poppins does its best work with strip-like, uniform lines and a tall, sturdy lowercase.
montserrat-merriweather: Montserrat draws its heading as a thread of ink with no swelling, crisp and wide-mouthed even when shrunk. Merriweather adds a stocky, cozy warmth.
playfair-inter: Dignified and literary, Playfair Display pairs hairline strokes with fat ones. Its best moments come big and short, while Inter stays out of its way.
quilon-switzer: Editorial swagger, then a quiet wire. Quilon flows with only slight thick-thin shifts, and Switzer follows with a plain, unshaded line and a tall waist that never swells, so a longer read glides along without a snag.
raleway-source-serif: Source Serif 4 reads dignified, with a gaping c and bowls that thin gently at the curve tops. Raleway's wire-like line glides above it, so the serif body feels anchored beneath a lighter, precise heading.
sentient-satoshi: Crisp, bookish, a bit guarded. Sentient keeps its round forms nearly shut and its strokes between monoline and hairline, while Satoshi opens right up with a soaring x-height and a wide e, so the two feel like closed door and open window.
space-grotesk-inter: Clean and geometric, Space Grotesk traces its lines as if with a single marker tip. And Inter sits next to it taller in the lowercase, with big breathing counters, so the heading feels compact beside a smoother, more spacious body.
special-elite-dm-sans: DM Sans reads friendly and approachable, its wide-set s terminals keeping things easy going. And Special Elite pushes back with a distressed, tall x-height that fills the line, the sort of look a dj name logo might borrow.
syne-general-sans: Syne's x-height climbs almost to cap height, drawn as a plain stripe of constant ink with no pinched curves. General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure and the same tall, line-filling x-height, so the sans-serif body follows smoothly behind.
young-serif-inter: Inter reads like a smooth tube, its big counters hollow and open. Young Serif brings a friendly, refined serif voice with low contrast, and beside Inter's rope-like uniformity it feels warmer and more lived in.
